summary:
IGNIS is an advanced web platform developed specifically for the NASA Space Apps Challenge to comprehensively unlock twenty-six years of NASA Physical Sciences Informatics microgravity combustion research spanning from 1997 to 2023. We successfully developed an integrated intelligence suite featuring an eighteen-investigation flight archive, a multi-pillar interactive flight timeline, advanced side-by-side comparison tools, and an intelligent SI Safety Engine that provides real-time Q&A and automated safety briefings. 
This platform directly addresses the core challenge by transforming complex, scattered physical science datasets into intuitive, highly actionable risk profiles across seven unique crewed environments—ranging from the International Space Station to lunar and Martian habitats, as well as specialized high-oxygen spacesuits 
As deep-space missions and Artemis-era architectures adopt higher cabin oxygen percentages, traditional Earth-derived fire safety models and material screening standards are no longer conservative or safe. IGNIS bridges this critical safety gap by empowering mission planners and aerospace engineers with empirical, data-driven synthesis to prevent catastrophic fire hazards before launch. By turning historical flight telemetry into accessible real-time insights, IGNIS ensures ultimate crew safety for the exciting future of sustainable human space exploration across the cosmos today.
details:
Project Details: IGNIS (Spacecraft Fire Safety Intelligence & Synthesis Engine)

1. What does it do & How does it work?

IGNIS is an intelligence and synthesis web application that decodes 26 years of NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion research (1997–2023).

Screenshot 2026-11-14 at 1.17.37 PM.png

  • How it works: It ingests and indexes 18 landmark flight investigations across 6 hardware platforms. The platform features an interactive Combustion Archive, a color-coded Flight Timeline (1997–2023), a Multi-Compare Tray for side-by-side analysis, and an SI Safety Engine & Q&A. Users select any of the 7 crewed environments (from the ISS to a 100% O2O_2O2​ spacesuit)to generate automated safety briefings, risk profiles, and real-time synthesis.
    Screenshot 2026-11-14 at 1.17.37 PM.png+ 4

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Instantaneous Synthesis: Eliminates the need for engineers to manually sift through decades of scattered technical reports and experimental logs.
  • Environment-Specific Risk Profiling: Calculates tailored risk scores and mitigation recommendations across 7 unique space habitats.
    Screenshot 2026-11-14 at 1.18.27 PM.png
  • Visual Data Storytelling: Turns complex physical telemetry into intuitive multi-environment risk radars, timeline distributions, and comparative flammability deltas.
    Screenshot 2026-11-14 at 1.17.54 PM.png+ 2

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

As Artemis-era missions and deep-space habitats adopt higher cabin oxygen percentages (30–34% O2O_2O2​), traditional Earth-derived material flammability screening is no longer conservative or safe. IGNIS bridges this critical safety gap by giving mission planners empirical, data-driven evidence to prevent catastrophic fire hazards before launch.

Screenshot 2026-11-14 at 1.17.37 PM.png

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Vite, Lucide Icons, HTML5.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic v2, custom deterministic SI Synthesis Engine.
  • Architecture & UI Design: Custom dark-mode space telemetry interface optimized for operational clarity and high-density data visualization.

5. How is your project creative?

IGNIS redefines how mission data is explored by introducing Super-Intelligence (SI) simulation to physical sciences. Instead of acting as a static document archive, IGNIS dynamically cross-references combustion physics (oxygen concentration, airflow speed, gravity levels, and fuel types) against specific habitat atmospheres, creating an interactive, generative safety workspace.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Operational Reality: Factored in real constraints of deep-space habitats (e.g., partial gravity, elevated oxygen, enclosed ventilation limits).
  • UI/UX for Crew & Engineers: Designed for high-pressure environments requiring immediate clarity, clean visual hierarchies, and fast access to critical safety margins.
